cohort: The study included 1,193 mothers of neonates in a neonatal unit, categorized into two groups: those aged 18-35 years (n=929) and those aged >= 35 years (n=264).
finding: Advanced maternal age (>=35 years) was significantly associated with an increased rate of gestational diabetes, preeclampsia, cesarean delivery, and meconium aspiration syndrome.
mod_finding: Advanced maternal age was associated with a statistically significant increase in the rate of cesarean delivery.
gest_age: Gestational week was measured, but no significant difference was found between maternal age groups.
